stories.title: FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c
stories.reason: Pure C99, zero-dependency implementation that runs the 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 model on a single CPU with just 8.24GB RAM (AVX2 SIMD, linear attention, MoE, MXFP4 quantization, no BLAS/ML framework). Running code, squarely about how models get served on constrained hardware, and not yet HN-front-paged (no points captured) — exactly the low-saturation discovery slot.
key_facts: Runs Kimi K3 (2.78T params) on one CPU, 8.24GB RAM, no GPU
Pure C99, no BLAS/ML framework dependency, AVX2 SIMD
Implements linear attention, MoE routing, MXFP4 quantization
8.8k GitHub stars, 1.4k forks

stories.title: GLM-5.3 and the spread of advanced cyber capabilities
stories.reason: Anthropic's own Frontier Red Team report: the open-weight GLM-5.3 crossed a real cyber-capability threshold — ~12% success on ExploitBench, found and chained real 0-days in a browser JS engine into a working file-read exploit, converted a disclosed Chrome CVE into a working exploit in ~20 min. Safety bypass rates for GLM-5.3 were 64%/92%/100% for deceptive-prompt/prefill/abliteration attacks vs 0% for safeguarded Claude models. NIST called it the most cyber-capable open-weight model released to date, ~4 months behind US frontier.
key_facts: GLM-5.3 (Zhipu/Z.ai) is open-weight with no meaningful safety restrictions
~12% success on ExploitBench (50/410), ~4% on Anthropic's internal Binary Exploitation benchmark — both thresholds essentially zero for earlier models
Found previously-unknown 0-days in a popular browser's JS engine, chained into a working arbitrary-file-read exploit
Turned a disclosed Chrome n-day into a working exploit chain in ~20 minutes of researcher time
Safety-bypass compliance: 64% (deceptive prompts), 92% (prefilled reasoning), 100% (abliteration) vs 0% for safeguarded Claude models across the same attacks
NIST assessment: most cyber-capable open-weight model to date, ~4 months behind US frontier capability

stories.title: ESP32S3 cluster running 1.58-bit (BitNet) Language model
stories.reason: A 0.4B BitNet (1.58-bit ternary) model distributed across 7 ESP32-S3 microcontrollers (1 master + 6 compute nodes) over an SPI daisy-chain, each node handling a slice of the transformer layers. No throughput numbers published, but a genuinely novel edge-serving architecture with running code at 143 HN points and low saturation.
key_facts: 7 ESP32-S3 boards: 1 master (tokenization/embedding/LM head) + 6 compute nodes (transformer layers 0-23)
0.4B parameter model, 1.58-bit ternary (BitNet) quantization
SPI daisy-chain interconnect between nodes; KV cache stored in PSRAM
No published latency/throughput numbers

stories.title: datawhalechina/zero-to-sglang
stories.reason: Datawhale/RadixArk's 'zero-to-sglang': a structured course that walks from inference fundamentals (KV cache, prefill/decode) through building a mini-SGLang inference engine to reading SGLang's real optimizations (attention backends, quantization). Solid free reference for serving internals; no single benchmark hook but directly on-topic for how models get served.
key_facts: Four-part course: inference fundamentals -> build a mini inference engine from scratch -> real SGLang optimizations -> contributing to SGLang
Includes a working 'mini-sglang' reference implementation with continuous batching and HTTP serving
Available in English and Chinese, partially complete
